correctness.rationale: The F16 multiplication and Frobenius presentation yields a 60-element rank-preserving action on the 2-dimensional building. Solomon–Tits yields a simply connected 2-dimensional covering building; Frobenius fixes the line F2·1, and Armstrong’s normal-closure formula combined with f a f^{-1}=a² kills both acting generators. An independent finite-field enumeration from the definition found 65 vertices, 315 edges, 315 triangles before quotient, and precisely 4,9,7 simplex orbits. The quotient CW complex has chi=2 and pi1=0, hence H2=Z with all other positive-dimensional homology zero; Hurewicz and Whitehead give S². A finite census alone would NOT prove pi1 or homotopy type.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The Resultary record “Integral topology of Singer quotients of rank-four finite-field buildings” computes cyclic Singer group G only; at q=2 it has pi1=Z/5, whereas the present full semilinear normalizer adds Frobenius and yields pi1=0. Thus that stronger-in-q theorem does not cover the larger acting group.
